scenes.say: Ever wondered how .NET apps manage to start quickly and still run efficiently? Let's break down the magic behind the scenes.

scenes.label: CLR
scenes.sub: The Common Language Runtime runs managed code.
scenes.say: First up, the Common Language Runtime, or CLR, is the engine that runs all managed .NET code.

rows.b: Turns IL into native code at runtime
Quick compile, then optimize hot code
Builds native code ahead of time

scenes.say: The Just-In-Time compiler, or JIT, converts intermediate code to native instructions as your app runs. Tiered compilation speeds up startup by compiling methods fast, then re-optimizing the busy ones. Ahead-Of-Time, or AOT, creates native code before you even launch the app, cutting startup delays.
Tiered JIT gives you a quick launch and tweaks performance as your app runs. AOT is all about instant startup, but it can't adapt as well after deployment.

scenes.question: Does AOT always outperform JIT?
scenes.right: No—AOT starts faster, but JIT can optimize code at runtime for better throughput.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Does Ahead-Of-Time compilation always beat Just-In-Time? Not quite. AOT gets you running fast, but JIT can actually deliver better performance over time by optimizing as your app runs.
